statement: Two-thirds of the pupils in a class are girls. A quarter of the girls wear glasses, and 4 girls wear glasses. How many pupils are in the class?

choices.misconception: I found the number of girls and stopped there instead of going on to the whole class.
I found the number of boys instead of the number of pupils in the whole class.
I used one third instead of two thirds when going from the girls to the whole class.
I doubled the 16 girls, as though the girls were half of the class.

hints: First find how many girls there are.
Work backwards through the fractions: the 4 girls are a known fraction of the girls, and the girls are a known fraction of the class. Undo one fraction at a time.
4 is a quarter of the girls, so there are 16 girls. 16 is two thirds of the class, so one third of the class is 8.

solutions.reliable: 4 girls are a quarter of the girls, so there are 16 girls. 16 is two thirds of the class, so one third is 8 and the whole class is 24. Check: two thirds of 24 is 16, and a quarter of 16 is 4. The transferable idea: undo fractions one layer at a time, finding one part before the whole.
solutions.elegant: The girls with glasses are a quarter of two thirds, that is one sixth, of the class. So the class has 6 x 4 = 24 pupils.

whyOnTest: Fractions of fractions are undone layer by layer, and each wrong choice stops at, or mishandles, one of the layers.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
